derivation: Take minus log of the supplied multivariate Gaussian density. The exponential gives +(1/2)theta^T Sigma^(-1)theta. The reciprocal prefactor gives (D/2)ln(2pi)+(1/2)ln|Sigma|.
checks: theta is Dx1; Sigma and its inverse are DxD; the quadratic is scalar.
The displayed ordinary density requires symmetric positive definite Sigma, hence positive determinant and invertibility.

derivation: Bayes gives -ln p(theta|X,y)=-ln p(y|X,theta)-ln p(theta)+ln p(y|X). The evidence is independent of theta.
Minimize L(theta)+(1/2)theta^T Sigma^(-1)theta+C, where L is the negative log likelihood and C=(D/2)ln(2pi)+(1/2)ln|Sigma|.
If the Gaussian observation noise is independent with a common fixed positive variance sigma^2, L=SSE/(2sigma^2)+(N/2)ln(2pi sigma^2). Constants may be omitted in the argmin.
subparts.conclusion: theta_MAP=argmin_theta {-ln p(y|X,theta)+(1/2)theta^T Sigma^(-1)theta}; including the prior normalization constant gives the same argmin.
checks: Gaussian prior normalization is preserved before dropping constants.
For a design X of size NxD, SSE=||y-Xtheta||^2 is scalar.
No numerical noise variance was supplied; the likelihood remains symbolic.

derivation: The x3 column in y1,y2,y3 order is (3,5,3)/100.
Let s=sum_n x_n count successes. Independence yields likelihood mu^s (1-mu)^(N-s).
Multiplying the Beta prior gives posterior kernel mu^(alpha+s-1)(1-mu)^(beta+N-s-1), for 0<mu<1.
Define a=alpha+s and b=beta+N-s. Integrating the kernel gives B(a,b), so normalization is 1/B(a,b)=Gamma(a+b)/(Gamma(a)Gamma(b)).
subparts.conclusion: mu | x_1..x_N ~ Beta(alpha+s,beta+N-s), with density mu^(alpha+s-1)(1-mu)^(beta+N-s-1)/B(alpha+s,beta+N-s) on (0,1).
checks: A proper Beta prior means alpha>0,beta>0; then posterior parameters remain positive for 0<=s<=N.
The density integrates to 1 by definition of the beta function.
No MAP formula is requested; boundary modes do not affect posterior validity.
